title: Internal Links
description: Linking within your own site, orphan pages, and why internal linking matters for SEO.
subject: html
html:
An internal link points to another page on the same website. They're what turn a pile of separate HTML files into one connected, navigable site.

Syntax

<a href="/notes/html/tables">Learn HTML Tables</a>

Basic Example

<p>New to HTML? Start with <a href="/notes/html/what-is-html">What is HTML?</a></p>

Browser output: a normal blue underlined link that keeps the visitor on the same site when clicked.

How It Works

Internal links are almost always written as relative URLs (usually root-relative, like /notes) since the domain is implied — see Relative URL. Together, a site's internal links form its overall structure, letting both users and search engine crawlers move from page to page.

Important Attributes

AttributePurpose
hrefThe internal destination path
targetAlmost never needed for internal links — opening your own site in a new tab is rarely good UX; see link-target

Real-World Example

<h2>Related HTML Notes</h2>
<ul>
    <li><a href="/notes/html/anchor-tag">The a Element</a></li>
    <li><a href="/notes/html/rel-attribute">rel Attribute</a></li>
</ul>

Exactly the "Related Notes" pattern used throughout this notes hub — internal links connecting each topic to the ones that build on it.

Common Mistakes

  • Broken internal links (linking to a page that's been renamed, moved, or deleted) — one of the most common and most damaging on-site errors
  • Orphan pages — pages that exist on the site but have no internal links pointing to them, making them hard for users and crawlers to discover at all
  • Vague repeated anchor text like "click here" for every internal link, wasting the chance to describe the destination

Best Practices

  • Regularly check for and fix broken internal links, especially after restructuring or renaming pages
  • Make sure every important page has at least one internal link pointing to it from somewhere on the site
  • Use descriptive anchor text that reflects the destination page's actual topic

Accessibility Considerations

Consistent, predictable internal navigation (the same menu structure, the same link wording for the same destination) helps all users, and especially screen reader or keyboard-only users, build a reliable mental model of the site.

SEO Considerations

Internal linking is a genuine, well-documented ranking factor — it helps search engines discover pages, understand the site's structure and topic hierarchy, and distribute "authority" between related pages. See Internal Linking (SEO) for the deeper strategy.

Browser & Modern HTML Notes

No special behavior — internal links work exactly like any other <a href>, just resolving to the same domain.

Mini Practice

  1. Add three internal links between related pages on a small sample site.
  2. Find (or imagine) a page on a site with no internal links pointing to it, and suggest where a link to it should be added.
